title: 2027 Jeep Grand Cherokee Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: Despite a major refresh for 2026, the Jeep Grand Cherokee greets the 2027 model year with several trim and equipment changes.
body_markdown:
The Jeep Grand Cherokee is a two-row midsize SUV that checks a lot of boxes, ranging from some off-road chops to near-luxury amenities. That means it competes with a wide range of vehicles, including the Honda Passport, the Ford Explorer, the Chevrolet Blazer, the Toyota 4Runner, the Mazda CX-70, and the Acura MDX. In its fifth generation, the Grand Cherokee was all-new for 2022, and the 2027 model year will have 10 trims: Laredo, Laredo X, Laredo Altitude, Laredo Upland, Limited, Limited Altitude, Limited Reserve, Trailhawk, Overland, and Summit.

## What’s New for the 2027 Jeep Grand Cherokee


The Grand Cherokee received a major refresh in 2026, including a revised grille, a new front bumper, updated LED lighting, upgraded tech, and a new powertrain, so the 2027 model year is largely a carryover with some new trims, fresh wheel designs, and new exterior colors. Both the Overland and Trailhawk trims return for 2027, and the Laredo Upland is completely new with a focus on value and Trailhawk-inspired looks. Base Laredo and Laredo X trims get a new standard 10.1-inch infotainment screen and the 4xe plug-in hybrid model has been dropped from the lineup.


## Design


The Grand Cherokee maintains Jeep’s signature upright design, and the updated grille and lighting signatures give it an elegant appearance. Standard wheels are 18 inches, with 20- and 21-inch wheels available on higher trims. Because each trim has its own design character, there are few appearance packages on the 2027 Grand Cherokee, but the top-tier Summit trim does offer a two-tone paint option as well as an Obsidian Package, which includes 21-inch black aluminum wheels, painted door cladding, and black exterior accents.


## Powertrain


There are just two powertrains available on the Grand Cherokee for the 2027 model year: the 3.6-liter V6 and the turbocharged 2.0-liter Hurricane four-cylinder. The Laredo and Laredo X come standard with the V6, and all other trims get the Hurricane four-cylinder. Rear-wheel drive (RWD) is standard, and four-wheel drive (4WD) is available on all trims. The maximum towing capacity is 6,200 pounds, and if you want the most off-road capability, look at the Trailhawk, which has 11.4 inches of ground clearance, an adaptive air suspension system, off-road driving modes, a two-speed transfer case, an integrated off-road camera system, and all-terrain tires. Depending on the engine and drivetrain, fuel economy ranges from 18 to 21 mpg in the city and from 25 to 26 mpg on the highway.


## Interior


The two-row Grand Cherokee seats five passengers and has 37.7 cubic feet of cargo space behind the second row, with a maximum capacity of 70.8 cubic feet. Cloth seats are standard, but leather seats are available on upper trims. A single-pane sunroof becomes standard starting on the Laredo X trim, and a dual-pane panoramic sunroof is available starting at the Limited trim. While the Laredo is fairly bare bones, the Laredo X gets standard heated front seats and a power liftgate.


## Technology


Standard tech features include a 10.1-inch infotainment screen, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a six-speaker sound system, a 10.25-inch digital cluster, dual-zone climate controls, front- and second-row USB ports, and a Wi-Fi hotspot (subscription required). Available features include a 12.3-inch infotainment screen, a 10.3-inch front-passenger screen, a head-up display, a wireless phone charger, ambient lighting, a nine-speaker Alpine audio system, a digital rearview mirror, a surround-view camera system, and night vision. A 19-speaker McIntosh premium audio system comes standard on the top-tier Summit trim.

## Safety


The base Grand Cherokee comes really well-equipped with standard safety features, including automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitors, rear cross-traffic alert, lane-keep assist, adaptive cruise control, a rear-view camera, and rear parking sensors. Available features include a surround-view camera system, parallel and perpendicular park assist, hands-free highway driving, and an intersection collision assist system. Neither the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) nor the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) had crash-tested the 2027 Grand Cherokee at the time of writing. However, NHTSA gave the 2026 model a five-star overall safety rating, and the IIHS gave it Good ratings in the side and small front overlap tests.


## Pricing and Release Date


The 2027 Jeep Grand Cherokee is expected to arrive in dealerships in late 2026. The full pricing spectrum hadn’t been announced at the time of writing, but Jeep said the entry-level 2027 Grand Cherokee Laredo would start at $41,515, including a $1,995 destination charge. The new Laredo Upland will start at $49,990, and the Trailhawk and Overland models will start at $54,995 and $57,895, respectively.
